estimates.outcome: Fraction of unique idea concepts (cosine-similarity overlap threshold 0.8)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Unique idea concepts divided by all idea entries in the condition pool; overlap is pairwise cosine similarity of Google Universal Sentence Encoder embeddings exceeding 0.8. A concept is a group of one or more ideas that do not overlap with other ideas in the set. One diversity level is defined per condition pool.

sources.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1108), diversity operationalization, left column below Fig. 1
sources.quote: when their pairwise cosine similarity exceeds the threshold of 0.8 (refs. 2,8). A unique idea concept is a group of one or more ideas that do not overlap with any other ideas in the set.

sources.locator: PDF p. 2 (printed p. 1108), Fig. 1 legend; Experiment 1 panel
sources.quote: The error bars show 95% confidence intervals for individual proportions.

estimates.notes: The eligible contrast is retained, but its numerical arm levels appear only as Figure 1 bar labels in the accessible article. These figure-only values were not transcribed under extraction rule 1. Interval endpoints, test statistics, p-values, SDs, SEs and effects are not printed in the accessible article text. The caption states the confidence level for both arms; ci_of=treatment_mean refers to the treatment arm interval, and the control arm has the same stated confidence level. No interval for the contrast is numerically available. Supplementary Table 1 could not be retrieved or checked. Person counts for this reanalysis remain null; original-study totals were not substituted. n_units is null because no number of analyzed sets is explicitly printed. The basis of the plotted intervals is not described in the accessible article. Numerical extraction is incomplete pending the supplement. The reanalysis says each participant submitted one idea, but the original Experiment 1 allowed several ideas in the same text box (Lee and Chung, PDF p. 6, printed p. 1911). How the diversity reanalysis handled these entries is unverified.

estimates.outcome: Number of ideas containing 'sprinkler' in each condition pool (raw count)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Count of idea entries in an entire condition pool that contain the word 'sprinkler'. This is the article's descriptive illustration of convergence on a single concept. Values are raw pool totals in ideas, not percentages or participant-level means.

sources.locator: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 1107), right column, first paragraph, Experiment 2A keyword-count illustration
sources.quote: 20 out of 96 ChatGPT-aided ideas included the word ‘sprinkler’, as opposed to only 7 in the web-search-aided condition and 12 in the human-only condition.

estimates.notes: The treatment_mean and control_mean fields hold the reported arm-level count statistic, as required for diversity arm levels; these are totals, not means over participants. unit=set reflects one count for each condition pool; the screening form used unit=output for the underlying idea-level keyword indicator. The source prints an idea denominator for the AI pool but none for either comparison pool. No denominator has been converted into a person count, no fraction or difference has been calculated, and no uncertainty is reported. n_units is null because the combined number of ideas in this contrast is not printed. A higher count indicates more ideas using this particular word; without comparison denominators, normalized convergence cannot be compared.

open_items: Obtain and read the separate Supplementary Information, then transcribe and verify every eligible contrast in Supplementary Table 1. Named publisher source: https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41562-025-02173-x/MediaObjects/41562_2025_2173_MOESM1_ESM.pdf

The primary unique-concept-fraction records currently contain no numerical arm levels or contrast statistics. Their Figure 1 bar labels were intentionally left untranscribed under extraction rule 1. Recover the table values and all confidence limits, tests, p-values and paper effects from the supplement.

Confirm analyzed people counts for each reanalysis and each arm against the supplement. The article prints no per-arm person counts; the keyword illustration prints ideas, not an explicit people count. Counts from the original paper or screening/data records were not copied into reanalysis fields.

Experiment 5 per-cell person counts are reported as missing from the supplement by the screening form; this needs direct confirmation. Do not compute counts from posted data during this transcription-only extraction.

Check whether the confidence intervals for differences in Supplementary Table 1 were adjusted for multiple comparisons. The Figure 1 legend describes Bonferroni-corrected intervals; the screening form flags a discrepancy with the table legend and corrected p-values that could not be checked here.

Confirm the analysis unit and uncertainty basis for every supplement outcome, including the uniqueness proportions, aggregated and pairwise similarities, and minimum-spanning-tree measure. Do not treat idea pairs as independent participants.

Resolve how the reanalysis treated original Experiment 1 text entries containing multiple ideas; the main article says one idea per participant, whereas the original Methods allowed multiple ideas in one response.

For the keyword illustration, the comparison-pool idea denominators and uncertainty are absent from the accessible article. The extracted levels are raw counts, so no percentage or standardized effect should be inferred.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-09. The entire markdown conversion was read sequentially, including the Reporting Summary. All pages of the local main PDF were read with pymupdf; every source quote was checked against its page text with whitespace normalization. No number was read from a figure, computed, inferred from a p-value or taken from screening notes. The only non-null outcome levels are the keyword totals explicitly printed in the article text; the stated confidence level for the primary figure intervals is retained from the figure legend. No outcome has a participant-level SE available from the accessed source. This is a secondary analysis of the six experiments screened as S1–S6, not a newly recruited sample. All share participants with c010, as confirmed in the main PDF p. 3 (printed p. 1109), Data availability, and PDF p. 5, Reporting Summary. Original-paper PDF consulted for inherited design metadata only: C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Lee and Chung (2024) - Empirical Investigation of ChatGPT on Creativity.pdf. Its Methods on PDF pp. 6–8 (printed pp. 1911–1913) confirm random individual assignment, online-panel recruitment in the USA, tasks, the factorial-cell assignments and the distinction between human-assisted and AI-only output. S1 and S4 used MTurk; the other studies used Prolific. Original-study sample counts were not substituted for unverified reanalysis counts. Preregistration fields refer to this secondary diversity analysis, for which no registration is stated. Model release year is null because this reanalysis does not identify a model version or its release year. Attempts to access the exact supplement URL named in the screening form and the named OSF project API (https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/zf3s2/files/osfstorage/) used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no personal identifier; both failed with WinError 10013. No supplement was found in the searched local literature, repository, temporary/download directories or D:/projects/ai-skill-atlas. The reconciliation and data-screening notes describe supplementary results but were not used as substitutes for directly checking the PDF. The supplement-only outcomes in not_extracted are unavailable, not judged ineligible. The extraction remains numerically incomplete pending that source. No independent extractor file was read. Only extraction/raw/c015.A.json was written.
